cards.title: La inversión negativa
cards.summary: En un registro formal, algunas expresiones negativas o restrictivas (never, rarely, not only, no sooner) van al principio de la oración y el auxiliar se coloca antes del sujeto, como en una pregunta.
cards.form: expresión negativa + auxiliar + sujeto + verbo: Never have I seen… · Not only did she…, but she also… · No sooner had I… than…
uses: Dar énfasis en discursos, informes y textos argumentativos.
Con never, rarely, seldom y little: Rarely do we see such talent.
Not only… but also: Not only did he apologize, but he also paid for the damage.
Condicionales formales sin if: Had I known, I would have called.

pitfalls.wrong: Never I have seen such a mess.
pitfalls.right: Never have I seen such a mess.
pitfalls.why: Después de la expresión negativa, el auxiliar va antes del sujeto.

pitfalls.wrong: Not only she apologized, but she also paid.
pitfalls.right: Not only did she apologize, but she also paid.
pitfalls.why: En presente y pasado simple se añade do, does o did, como en una pregunta.

pitfalls.wrong: No sooner had I arrived when it started to rain.
pitfalls.right: No sooner had I arrived than it started to rain.
pitfalls.why: No sooner va con than, no con when.

pitfalls.wrong: If had I known, I would have called.
pitfalls.right: Had I known, I would have called.
pitfalls.why: En la condicional invertida desaparece if.

examples.en: Rarely do we get a second chance like this.
examples.es: Pocas veces tenemos una segunda oportunidad como esta.

examples.en: Not only did the plan fail, but it also cost a fortune.
examples.es: El plan no solo fracasó, sino que además costó una fortuna.

examples.en: No sooner had we sat down than the lights went out.
examples.es: Apenas nos habíamos sentado cuando se apagaron las luces.

examples.en: Under no circumstances should you share your password.
examples.es: Bajo ninguna circunstancia debes compartir tu contraseña.

examples.en: Had I known about the meeting, I would have attended.
examples.es: Si hubiera sabido lo de la reunión, habría asistido.

examples.en: Little did they know that the company was about to close.
examples.es: No tenían ni idea de que la empresa estaba a punto de cerrar.

cards.title: Cleft sentences: What I need is…
cards.summary: Para destacar una parte de la oración, el inglés la separa con What… is… o It is / It was… that…, como el español «lo que necesito es…» o «fue ella quien…».
cards.form: What + sujeto + verbo + is / was + lo destacado · It is / It was + lo destacado + that / who…
uses: Destacar una información: What I need is more time.
Corregir o contrastar: It was the price, not the quality, that worried customers.
Con all, «lo único que»: All I want is a quiet weekend.
It was not until… that…: It was not until I moved abroad that I understood my own culture.

pitfalls.wrong: What I need it is more time.
pitfalls.right: What I need is more time.
pitfalls.why: La parte con what ya es el sujeto: no se repite con it.

pitfalls.wrong: It was my sister who she called.
pitfalls.right: It was my sister who called.
pitfalls.why: Después de who o that no se repite el sujeto.

pitfalls.wrong: The thing what I need is time.
pitfalls.right: The thing I need is time.
pitfalls.why: Después de un sustantivo se usa that, which o nada, nunca what.

pitfalls.wrong: It were the students who complained.
pitfalls.right: It was the students who complained.
pitfalls.why: En It is / It was, el verbo va siempre en singular.

examples.en: What surprised me was how calm she remained.
examples.es: Lo que me sorprendió fue lo tranquila que se mantuvo.

examples.en: It was the price, not the quality, that worried customers.
examples.es: Fue el precio, y no la calidad, lo que preocupó a los clientes.

examples.en: It was not until I moved abroad that I understood my own culture.
examples.es: No entendí mi propia cultura hasta que me mudé al extranjero.

examples.en: All I want is a quiet weekend.
examples.es: Lo único que quiero es un fin de semana tranquilo.

examples.en: What we should do is ask for a second opinion.
examples.es: Lo que deberíamos hacer es pedir una segunda opinión.

examples.en: It was her teacher who encouraged her to write.
examples.es: Fue su profesora quien la animó a escribir.

cards.title: Hedging: suavizar afirmaciones
cards.summary: En textos académicos y argumentativos, el inglés suaviza las afirmaciones para no sonar demasiado categórico: seem, appear, tend to, may, it could be argued that.
cards.form: It could be argued that… · seem / appear + to + verbo · tend to + verbo · may (well) + verbo · be likely to + verbo
uses: Presentar una opinión con prudencia: It could be argued that…
Indicar una tendencia, no una regla: People tend to…
Expresar probabilidad: The results are likely to change.
Distanciarse de una afirmación: The policy appears to have failed.

pitfalls.wrong: It could be argue that the law is unfair.
pitfalls.right: It could be argued that the law is unfair.
pitfalls.why: Es una pasiva: could be + participio (argued).
Tend to va seguido del infinitivo, sin -ing.

pitfalls.wrong: The plan seems that it has failed.
pitfalls.right: The plan seems to have failed.
pitfalls.why: Con el sujeto real se usa seem to; con that, el sujeto es it (It seems that…).
Probable no admite be + to + verbo: se usa likely.

examples.en: It could be argued that the reform came too late.
examples.es: Se podría argumentar que la reforma llegó demasiado tarde.

examples.en: Young people tend to share more information online.
examples.es: Los jóvenes suelen compartir más información en internet.

examples.en: The new policy appears to have reduced traffic.
examples.es: La nueva política parece haber reducido el tráfico.

examples.en: The results may well change once more data is available.
examples.es: Es muy posible que los resultados cambien cuando haya más datos.

examples.en: Prices are likely to rise again next year.
examples.es: Es probable que los precios vuelvan a subir el año que viene.

examples.en: There seems to be some confusion about the rules.
examples.es: Parece haber cierta confusión sobre las normas.

cards.title: La nominalización
cards.summary: El inglés formal convierte verbos y adjetivos en sustantivos (decide → decision, fail → failure) para condensar ideas y dar un tono más objetivo.
cards.form: verbo / adjetivo → sustantivo: decide → decision, fail → failure, grow → growth, able → ability · the + sustantivo + of: the introduction of the law
uses: Condensar ideas: The government's decision to raise taxes…
Dar un tono impersonal y académico: The failure of the talks surprised everyone.
Suele ir con of o con un posesivo: the growth of cities, the city's growth.

pitfalls.why: Después de un posesivo va un sustantivo (decision), no el verbo (decide).

pitfalls.wrong: The fail of the project was expensive.
pitfalls.right: The failure of the project was expensive.
pitfalls.why: El sustantivo de fail es failure.

pitfalls.wrong: The grow of the city has been fast.
pitfalls.right: The growth of the city has been fast.
pitfalls.why: El sustantivo de grow es growth.

pitfalls.wrong: There has been an increase of prices.
pitfalls.right: There has been an increase in prices.
pitfalls.why: Increase, rise y fall van con in para indicar lo que aumenta o baja.

examples.en: The introduction of the new law caused a lot of debate.
examples.es: La entrada en vigor de la nueva ley generó mucho debate.

examples.en: The failure of the talks surprised everyone.
examples.es: El fracaso de las negociaciones sorprendió a todos.

examples.en: There has been a sharp increase in unemployment.
examples.es: Ha habido un fuerte aumento del desempleo.

examples.en: Her refusal to comment only made things worse.
examples.es: Su negativa a hacer comentarios solo empeoró las cosas.

examples.en: The rapid growth of cities puts pressure on housing.
examples.es: El rápido crecimiento de las ciudades ejerce presión sobre la vivienda.

examples.en: Their ability to adapt is remarkable.
examples.es: Su capacidad de adaptación es extraordinaria.

items.term: Never have I… / Not only did… but also…
items.es: inversión negativa: nunca he…, no solo…, sino que también…

items.term: What I need is… / It was… that…
items.es: oraciones escindidas: lo que necesito es…, fue… quien / lo que…

items.term: It could be argued that… / tend to / appear to
items.es: suavizar afirmaciones: se podría argumentar que…, suele…, parece…
nominalización: convertir verbos y adjetivos en sustantivos
